title: Perfect ordinary realization and scalar extension at an algebraically closed point
statement:
Let $p$ be prime, $k$ an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and $u:A\to B$ a unital homomorphism of finite commutative rings annihilated by integers prime to $p$. Use ordinary uncompleted derived categories of constant module sheaves on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Let $D^b_{ctf}(s,A)$ mean bounded constructible complexes of finite Tor amplitude [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude], with the finite-ring etale-origin convention [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin]. Write $T_s(M)=M\otimes_A^LB$ for ordinary derived change of rings [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], and let $\Gamma_s$ be sections over the final object, applied termwise on complexes [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]. An ordinary perfect $A$-complex means a complex isomorphic to a bounded complex of finitely generated projective $A$-modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex].

For every $M\in D^b_{ctf}(s,A)$, the ordinary complex $\Gamma_sM$ is perfect, and the canonical sections--tensor comparison is an isomorphism
$$S_M:(\Gamma_sM)\otimes_A^LB\xrightarrow{\sim}\Gamma_s(T_sM).$$
It is natural in $M$, is the identity for $u=\operatorname{id}_A$, and is compatible with composition of finite coefficient maps under the derived associativity identifications. In particular, on a bounded complex of constant sheaves associated to finite projective $A$-modules, $S_M$ is the class of the termwise map $\Gamma_s(F)\otimes_A B\to\Gamma_s(F\otimes_A B)$ sending $x\otimes b$ to the section $x\otimes b$.

source.place: Final sentence, naturality in the coefficient ring, and the compact-cohomology/stalk clause of the statement; agent extraction of the point-realization argument in returned Step 4. No separate point-realization paragraph occurs in the blueprint proof.

proof.text: Write $c_R$ for termwise constant realization. First identify its unit on modules at $s$. For any $R$-module $V$ with discrete topology, $U\mapsto C(|U|,V)$ is a sheaf by [lem-cbc-continuous-functions-fpqc-sheaf], since the pro-etale coverings are fpqc [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. The constant-presheaf map to this sheaf is locally surjective: the open fibres of a locally constant function cover $U$. It is locally injective: on a nonempty $U$ equal constant functions have equal values, and on the empty scheme use its empty covering. Thus [lem-cbc-set-presheaf-sheafification-local-bijection] identifies its sheafification with this function sheaf. This identification respects addition and the constant-ring action by [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface]. At $U=s$, a function on the one-point space is a unique constant. Consequently the constant-value map $\eta_V:V\to\Gamma_s c_R(V)$ is an isomorphism, natural in every linear map. This applies to arbitrary modules, not just finite ones, and to every coefficient ring used below. For finite $R$, functions into the discrete ring factor through connected components, and continuity is equivalent by the quotient topology; this also identifies the coefficient sheaf specified in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] with the constant ring sheaf.

source.place: Lemma 4.2.12, discrete case, p. 30; explicit local-bijection verification

proof.text: The constant-presheaf/evaluation adjunction extends to module sheaves by [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-interface]: a map $V\to F(s)$ assigns on $U$ the restriction of that section along $U\to s$, and conversely a sheaf map is evaluated on constant sections at $s$. These operations are inverse. This gives $c_R\dashv\Gamma_s$, with counit $\epsilon_F:c_R\Gamma_sF\to F$ sending a constant section $x$ to $x|_U$. The functor $c_R$ is exact by [def-sfb-site-derived-constant-module-functor] and $\Gamma_s$ is exact by [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact]. Hence the termwise unit and counit descend to derived categories, with their naturality and triangle identities, by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. The unit remains an isomorphism by step 1. In particular $\Gamma_s c_R(C)\cong C$ for every ordinary complex $C$.

source.place: Tag 03CY, lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules; Tag 093J, lemma-constant-exact; derived localization of the explicit unit and counit

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin], choose a bounded constructible etale complex $L$ with $\nu_s^*L\cong M$. The exact equivalence of [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-pullback-stalk](1) identifies etale $A$-module sheaves at the algebraically closed point with ordinary $A$-modules, with inverse the constant sheaf functor: its counit is the natural constant-sheaf isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-algebraically-closed-etale-sheaf-constant], which respects the module operations by naturality. Apply these inverse equivalences termwise to obtain $L\cong c_{A,\mathrm{et}}C_0$, where $C_0=\Gamma(s_{\mathrm{et}},L)$. By [lem-sfb-geometric-inverse-image-constant-module], $\nu_s^*c_{A,\mathrm{et}}C_0\cong c_AC_0$ termwise, hence $M\cong c_AC_0$. The counit of step 2 is an isomorphism on every such object: on $c_AC_0$ its inverse is $c_A\eta_{C_0}$ by the triangle identity. Thus, putting $C=\Gamma_sM$, the specified natural counit $\epsilon_M:c_AC\xrightarrow{\sim}M$ is an isomorphism; no choice of an etale origin enters this specified map.

source.place: Tag 09AL, lemma-compare-constructible-derived; etale-cohomology.tex Tag 04JQ, lemma-equivalence-abelian-sheaves-point; sites.tex Tag 0H7J, constant objects under inverse image

proof.text: The complex $C$ is bounded with finite cohomology modules. Indeed the exact point equivalence in step 3 takes the bounded constructible cohomology of $L$ to finite $A$-modules: a constructible sheaf on the one-point scheme is locally constant with finite module value, and this value is its stalk, which [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-pullback-stalk] identifies with sections. Equivalently apply the cohomology formula in [lem-weil-point-proetale-sections-exact] to $M\cong c_AC_0$. The finite ring $A$ is Noetherian, since any ideal is generated by its finite set of elements.

source.place: Tag 09AL and the bounded constructible convention; elementary finite-ring Noetherian check

proof.text: Constant realization commutes with ordinary tensor products. To see the actual map, a bilinear map of constant modules into a sheaf $H$ is, by the adjunction in step 2, precisely an $R$-bilinear map $V\times W\to\Gamma_sH$: the two descriptions agree on constant local sections, which locally generate the constant sheaves. The tensor universal property [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] therefore gives the unique isomorphism $c_R(V)\otimes_{R_s}c_R(W)\cong c_R(V\otimes_RW)$ taking $v\otimes w$ to the constant section $v\otimes w$. The functor $c_R$ preserves direct sums because it is a left adjoint, so these maps also identify total tensor complexes, with differential $d(v\otimes w)=dv\otimes w+(-1)^{\deg v}v\otimes dw$.

source.place: Section 03EK, tensor universal property; constant-sheaf adjunction of step 2

proof.text: Let $V$ be any ordinary $A$-module. Choose K-flat resolutions with flat terms of $C$ and $V[0]$ using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution] on the one-object site. Their constant realizations are K-flat with flat terms by clause (1) of [lem-sfb-constant-realization-derived-scalar-extension], applied also to the identity coefficient map. The ordinary tensor calculation [lem-pc-source-kflat-module-tensor-model], the sheaf tensor calculation [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent], and step 5 give $c_A(C\otimes_A^LV)\cong c_AC\otimes_{A_s}^Lc_AV\cong M\otimes_{A_s}^Lc_AV$. Choose a Tor interval $[a,b]$ for $M$ as in [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude]. The last complex has no cohomology outside $[a,b]$, since $c_AV$ is a degree-zero module sheaf. Apply the exact $\Gamma_s$ and the unit isomorphism of step 2. It follows that $H^q(C\otimes_A^LV)=0$ for $q\notin[a,b]$. Since $V$ was arbitrary, this is ordinary finite Tor amplitude for $C$. No conservativity of sections on arbitrary pro-etale sheaves is asserted or needed.

source.place: Tags 06YS, 0G7E and 06YU; K-flat calculation of ordinary and sheaf tensor, followed by the Tor test

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-pseudocoherent-cohomology-criterion], step 4 makes $C$ pseudo-coherent over the commutative Noetherian ring $A$. Step 6 verifies the finite Tor dimension hypothesis for every ordinary module, so [lem-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-finite-tor-perfect] gives an isomorphism $P\cong C$ in $D(A)$ for a bounded complex $P$ of finitely generated projective $A$-modules. This is precisely the ordinary perfectness required by [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Neither locality of $A$ nor freeness of these projectives is assumed.

Use [lem-sfb-constant-realization-derived-scalar-extension] for $u:A\to B$ and $C=\Gamma_sM$, with its specified isomorphism $\kappa_C:T_s(c_AC)\xrightarrow{\sim}c_B(C\otimes_A^LB)$. Define
$$S_M=\Gamma_s(T_s\epsilon_M)\circ\Gamma_s(\kappa_C^{-1})\circ\eta_{C\otimes_A^LB}.$$
Its source is $C\otimes_A^LB$ and its target is $\Gamma_sT_sM$. Each factor is an isomorphism: $\eta$ by step 2, $\kappa$ by the cited theorem, and $T_s\epsilon_M$ by step 3 and the functoriality of [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. This constructs the comparison without choosing a projective model or an etale origin. Each factor is natural in $M$, so the displayed formula is natural in $M$.

source.place: Tag 0G7E and Tag 0D6D, constant-realization scalar comparison; explicit mate under the constant/sections adjunction

proof.text: To identify this with the canonical sections--tensor map, use $P\cong C$ from step 7 and the natural isomorphism $c_AP\cong M$ from step 3. Projective modules are flat by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat], and $P$ is K-flat by [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat]. Clause (1) of [lem-sfb-constant-realization-derived-scalar-extension] makes $c_AP$ K-flat and computes its coefficient change termwise; [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] computes the ordinary change on $P$ termwise as well. In the formula of step 8 the unit sends $x\otimes b$ to its constant section, $\kappa^{-1}$ identifies that section with the tensor of the two constant sections, and the counit restricts $x$ to the given sheaf. Thus the resulting chain map is exactly $\Gamma_s(c_AP)\otimes_AB\to\Gamma_s(c_AP\otimes_{A_s}B_s)$, $x\otimes b\mapsto x\otimes b$. The maps commute with differentials by bilinearity. This proves the asserted normalization on every bounded finite-projective constant complex, as well as identifying the comparison on $M$ by its natural construction.

source.place: Tag 0G7E and K-flat computation; more-algebra.tex Tag 064K; explicit pure-tensor calculation

proof.text: For the identity map, the formula of step 9 sends $x\otimes a$ to the section $ax$, so under both tensor unit identifications it is the identity. For $A\xrightarrow{u}B\xrightarrow{v}D$, each $P^i\otimes_AB$ is finite projective over $B$: choose finitely many generators, split the resulting surjection $A^r\to P^i$ by projectivity, and tensor its splitting to get a splitting from $B^r$. The resulting bounded complex $c_B(P\otimes_AB)$ represents $T_sM$ by step 9. It lies in $D^b_c(s,B)$: by [lem-sfb-geometric-inverse-image-constant-module] it is termwise $\nu_s^*$ of the constant etale complex with the same finite $B$-modules, whose cohomology sheaves are constant with finite values on the one stratum $s$. If $P$ lives in degrees $[a,b]$, it has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$: it is K-flat with flat terms by clause (1) of [lem-sfb-constant-realization-derived-scalar-extension]; for a degree-zero $B_s$-module $N$ take a flat-term K-flat resolution $F\to N$ [lem-pc-kflat-resolution], so [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] computes the derived tensor by $\operatorname{Tot}(c_B(P\otimes_AB)\otimes F)$, quasi-isomorphic to the termwise tensor with $N$ since tensoring with a K-flat complex keeps the cone of $F\to N$ acyclic; that complex vanishes outside $[a,b]$. Thus the successive comparisons have their stated domains. So these models compute the successive changes. On a generator $(x\otimes b)\otimes d$, both the successive sections maps and the map for $v\circ u$, under associativity, give the section $x\otimes v(b)d$. Hence the chain maps agree. Clause (3) of [lem-sfb-constant-realization-derived-scalar-extension] identifies these associativity maps with the specified derived transitivity identifications; naturality of $\epsilon$ and the triangle identities from step 2 cancel the intermediate constant/sections unit and counit. This gives the composition law for $M$, independently of the model.

source.place: Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition; explicit identity and successive coefficient calculations on the bounded projective model
